actions.name: Spend from a Bitcoin FROST account (looks single-sig)
actions.summary: t of the ceremony's n participants spend the account's coins in two rounds. The witness is ONE BIP-340 signature by the key-path output key: to the chain it is a single-sig taproot spend — no policy, no signers.

fields.name: inputs
fields.means: the coins spent, each with its prevout (value + scriptPubKey)

fields.name: outputs
fields.means: the payee first, then change back to the account unless dust

fields.name: fee
fields.means: declared, must equal inputs − outputs; sized for one 64-byte signature per input

steps.does: Chooses the account ('btc-frost@<CAIP-10>', coordinate_set_policy) and calls coordinate_propose_btc_spend(pay_to, amount_sat, fee_rate). The module needs Settings → btc-rpc (the user's own Bitcoin Core node): it reads the account's coins with scantxoutset, keeps only coins whose scriptPubKey is the account's, and builds the spend largest coin first until the payment and its fee are covered — payee first, change back to the account unless it would be dust (then it goes to the fee). The fee is fee_rate × an upper bound of the signed vsize and is declared as inputs − outputs. Every input carries its prevout (amount + scriptPubKey). The driver's gate runs before anything is published; then the policy, the effect, and the context are published (environment = the chain's CAIP-2 bip122:<genesis>, account = the account's address, slot = the intent id, expiry), and the coin read is recorded in the log as an external read (source 'bitcoind:scantxoutset'), so every signer can account for the inputs (invariant 10). The materialization every member re-derives: dCBOR ['bip341.keypath.frost-bip445.v1', <CAIP-2 chain>, [each input's BIP-341 key-path SigMsg]].

steps.who: each member who is a participant — Approve once
steps.does: Round 1 (Approve): the keystore commits fresh nonces for this intent under the ceremony's label and the member publishes its public nonces, one per input, named by its host key, attested by the host key over P. The core advances to round 2 at t. Round 2 (automatic, on the room's tick): the signer SET is what the log fixes — the first t round-1 contributions the fold accepts, in canonical order — so honest members agree on it; each member in it has its keystore make a partial signature per input under that set's aggregate nonce and publishes {r: 2, signer, set, psigs}, attested. A member outside the set is told 'not-in-signing-set' and publishes nothing. A nonce is consumed before it is used; a keystore restarted between the rounds has lost it and refuses round 2 — the session aborts rather than reuse a nonce.
steps.signs: round 1: nothing (public nonces); round 2: a BIP-445 partial signature per input over its BIP-341 key-path SigMsg (hash_type 0x00, every input's amount and scriptPubKey, spend_type = key path), valid only under the carried signer set; each contribution attested by the member's host key over P

steps.who: any member, through their own Bitcoin node
steps.does: coordinate_submit: the settlement re-runs the driver's gate, finds a signer set with all t partials, aggregates them into one BIP-340 signature per input and verifies each under x(Q) before building anything. The witness of every input is that signature alone. Broadcast through the user's node.
steps.signs: nothing new — t partial signatures aggregate into one

steps.who: no one — the node is read
steps.does: Final at the network's confirmation depth, read from the node. On chain the input's witness is one 64-byte signature, the shape Bitcoin Core's own single-sig taproot spend has.

refusals.what: a spend with an input that is not this account's coins, or a declared fee that is not inputs − outputs
refusals.why: the same gate as the script multisigs, before anyone signs

refusals.what: a round-1 contribution from a non-participant, or a round-1 payload offered in round 2
refusals.why: the driver checks the signer is a participant and the round tag

refusals.what: a round-2 partial that is tampered, from a signer outside its carried set, or under a set of the wrong size
refusals.why: the partial verifies only against its set and the signer's public share

refusals.what: a round-2 contribution from a member outside the log's signer set
signing round 2 after a restart between the rounds
refusals.why: the nonce is gone and is never regenerated for the same session: 'refused … abort', nothing published
the keystore consumes a nonce before use and refuses a second use
no complete signer set: 'insufficient-signatures'; below t there is no spend

refusals.what: an aggregate that does not verify under the account key
refusals.why: settlement verifies every aggregate before building a transaction

actions.ui: Room → + → Payment → Settles via Bitcoin (FROST) → From <account> → payee + amount (sat) + fee (sat/vB) → Propose; card → Approve once (round 2 follows on the tick). The card also offers 'Sign outside muster (PSBT)', which answers no-outside-format for a FROST intent. Settle is headless (coordinate_submit).

claims.claim: The chain sees one signature by one key: nothing on chain names the policy, the threshold, or who signed
Shares and nonces live only in each member's keystore; a nonce is never reused, and a restart aborts the session
Every signer inside the room is named by its host key; the room sees who took part
The user's node learns the account's address when the proposer reads its coins, and sees the signed spend first
BIP-445 and ChillDKG are drafts; this port is demo-grade and not constant time

evidence.what: BIP-340: the one Schnorr signature the chain checks

unverified: The btc-frost driver is not run through checkConformance by any test (only its profile, in profile_test); CLAUDE.md's working agreement says conformance grades every driver.
The card body draws only to / value, so it shows no outputs for a btc-spend (Room.qml cardFor), and the ready box's 'Nothing settles on-chain' is wrong for this rail.

coordinate_submit polls the node for about four seconds; if the spend is not final by then it returns pending, and nothing later publishes the final event for a Bitcoin intent (only LEZ settles are re-watched by the pump). From reading nim-lib/muster_module.nim, not a test.

The room's fold counts one approval per contributor NAME in the event key, not per verifying key, so the room can show 'executable' early if one signature is published under two names (seen in a scratch run against the threshold driver, not a repo test). The settlement re-counts by the key that signed, so nothing wrong settles.

actions.name: Make a FROST key (ChillDKG ceremony in the room)
actions.summary: The setup for this family: t-of-n members run a ChillDKG key ceremony over the room's log. The room is the authenticated coordinator ChillDKG asks for, and every member computes the coordinator's steps from the log. The result is one threshold key; the taproot address it gives is disclosed into the room with the ceremony's public recovery data.

fields.name: ceremony_id
fields.means: a name for the key, without '/'

fields.name: network
fields.means: a Bitcoin network name — regtest (the default), signet, testnet or mainnet; the account is on that network

fields.name: n
fields.means: participants, n ≥ 2 — the first n members to join, in the log's order

agreement.threshold: all n participants: the ceremony completes only when every participant's step-1 and step-2 messages are in the log; a fault aborts it (ChillDKG is not robust)
agreement.finality: immediate — in the room, when each participant finalizes and discloses

disclosure.field: step messages (encrypted shares, VSS commitments, certifying signatures)
account + recovery data (host keys, t, threshold key, public shares)

steps.does: frost_ceremony_open(ceremony_id, network, t, n): the module checks n ≥ 2, 1 ≤ t ≤ n and an id without '/', publishes frost/<id>/open {network, t, n}, and joins it.

frost_ceremony_join: the keystore derives a host key for label 'frost/<id>' from its own secret — never exported — and the member publishes frost/<id>/join/<member> {host}, author-signed. The first n joins in the log's canonical order are the participants.
steps.signs: an Ed25519 author signature (room identity) over the join event

steps.who: each participant — automatically, on the room's tick
steps.does: Step 1: once n have joined, the keystore makes the participant's step-1 message — its secret shares for every participant, encrypted to their host keys, a VSS commitment and a proof of possession — published as frost/<id>/pmsg1/<host>. Step 2: once all n step-1 messages are in the log, each participant computes the coordinator's step 1 from the log itself (the room only relays) and its keystore makes the step-2 message: its certifying signature (CertEq) over the ceremony's transcript, published as frost/<id>/pmsg2/<host>.
steps.signs: step 2: the participant's certifying signature (CertEq) by its host key

steps.does: Once all n step-2 messages are in the log, each computes the coordinator's finalize from the log — the certificate and the recovery data — and its keystore checks the certificate. Then it discloses the account, author-signed, with config {ceremony, recovery}: the address is bech32m OP_1 x(Q) — ChillDKG's threshold key is already a taproot output key (it commits to an unspendable script path), so it is used as it stands. Any member re-derives the account from the recovery data, with no chain read; a member's share is recovered from the same public data by its keystore, never stored.

refusals.what: a disclosure whose address does not derive from its recovery data
refusals.why: the account is the ceremony, re-derived; a mismatch is refused, never trusted

refusals.what: a faulty ceremony message: a bad commitment, proof, share, or a coordinator's lie
refusals.why: ChillDKG raises with the blamed participant; the ceremony does not complete

refusals.what: a join published in another member's name
refusals.why: joins are author-signed; the room's read path drops a forged one

refusals.what: a share or a nonce in the log
refusals.why: none is ever published: the ceremony's entries are its open, joins and step messages

actions.ui: Room → Accounts → 'FROST key ceremony (Bitcoin taproot)' → a name, t, n, network (regtest by default) → Open the ceremony and join it; other members → Join. It advances on the room's tick and the account appears under Accounts.

claims.claim: No share and no nonce enters the log; a share is recovered from the public recovery data by the member's own keystore
The room coordinates: every member computes the coordinator's steps from the log — there is no coordinator server
To anyone outside the room the account is one key: its address names no policy and no signers
ChillDKG aborts on a fault; a participant who stops answering stops the ceremony
The participants are the first n members to join, in the log's order — the opener does not choose them
Demo-grade: this FROST code is not constant time and sits behind the production gate

unverified: The hosted checks on t, n and the id, and 'not-a-participant' for a member who joins after the first n, are from reading nim-lib/muster_module.nim and coordination/aggregate.nim; no test covers them.
